paper: FactorMAD: A Multi-Agent Debate Framework Based on Large Language Models for Interpretable Stock Alpha Factor Mining
claim_boundary: A researcher-authored monthly U.S.-stock analogue of FactorMAD in which two deterministic agents alternate proposal and critique over interpretable factor programs, a validator/corrector enforces predictive and diversity gates, and 100 accepted factors feed a training-only linear prediction model; not the missing prompts, GPT-4o calls, native factors, A-share data, or models.

primary_source_anchors.mechanism: Two differently initialized agents alternate factor summaries, critiques, and improved proposals, starting from either an existing or generated seed.
Each proposed factor is generated, validated, corrected for at most K iterations, evaluated for predictive quality and correlation, and admitted only if both gates pass.
The factor development pipeline enforces error-free execution, no look-ahead, stationarity, dimension consistency, output format, and low correlation with the existing library.
One hundred mined factors feed LR, MLP, and LightGBM return models; the investment simulation uses LR predictions to select a Top-50 portfolio.
Ten debate iterations improve factor quality relative to a single-agent loop while keeping factors concise and interpretable.

debate_policy.agent_a_perspective: maximize absolute mean RankIC and RankICIR
debate_policy.agent_b_perspective: retain predictive quality while minimizing accepted-factor correlation and expression complexity
debate_policy.neighbor_rule: candidate shares at least one seed component with the current proposal; a correction may choose the best admissible unused neighbor
debate_policy.feedback_used: training-only mean RankIC, RankICIR, expression complexity, and correlation with accepted-factor RankIC histories

prediction_model.weight_normalization: divide coefficients by total absolute coefficient weight
prediction_model.common_portfolio_adapter: the frozen linear prediction score enters fixed value-weighted long-short deciles and all six common paths

preserved_elements: two agents with distinct initial perspectives
accepted factors persist into the factor library
approximated_elements: JKP characteristics replace daily A-share OHLCV and VWAP
a finite symbolic grammar replaces unconstrained GPT-4o Python generation
deterministic quality and diversity objectives replace missing role prompts
RankIC-history neighbors replace natural-language debate context
one correction step replaces the unavailable correction agent and validator
one-month excess returns replace the ten-day future-VWAP label
training-only ridge regression replaces the undisclosed LR implementation
common monthly deciles replace overlapping daily Top-50 ten-day sleeves
invented_elements: the twelve seed characteristics and 210-program grammar
the RankIC quality and diversity scoring formulas
the ridge penalty and coefficient normalization
